# Two-group sample size calculation for repeated measures (participant averages)
# Analyzing participant means with pooled t-test

# Study parameters
marginal_SD <- 1          # Marginal SD of the outcome
ICC <- 0.4               # Intraclass correlation
k <- 4                   # Observations per participant
mean_diff <- 0.45        # Constant group mean difference
alpha <- 0.05            # Significance level
target_power <- 0.90     # Target power
allocation_ratio <- 1    # Equal allocation (1:1)

# Step 1: Calculate effective SD of participant averages
# When averaging k observations with ICC structure:
# Var(participant_mean) = (marginal_SD)^2 / k * [1 + (k-1)*ICC]

effective_var <- (marginal_SD^2 / k) * (1 + (k - 1) * ICC)
effective_SD <- sqrt(effective_var)

cat("=== Effective SD of Participant Averages ===\n")
cat("Marginal SD:", marginal_SD, "\n")
cat("ICC:", ICC, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Effective variance of participant mean:", effective_var, "\n")
cat("Effective SD of participant mean:", effective_SD, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Set up power calculation
# For a two-sample t-test comparing participant means:
# Under H0: μ1 = μ2
# Under HA: μ1 - μ2 = mean_diff
# 
# With equal allocation (n per group), the pooled SD is effective_SD
# The test statistic is t = (mean1 - mean2) / (SD_pooled * sqrt(2/n))
# where SD_pooled ≈ effective_SD (both groups have same marginal structure)
#
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = mean_diff / (effective_SD * sqrt(2/n))
# df = 2*n - 2

# Function to calculate power given n per group
calc_power <- function(n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  # Standard error of difference: SE = effective_SD * sqrt(2/n)
  SE_diff <- effective_SD * sqrt(2 / n)
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- mean_diff / SE_diff
  # Critical value (two-sided)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  # Power: P(|T| > t_crit | H_A)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Step 3: Find minimum n that achieves target power
# Search over a reasonable range
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) calc_power(n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha))

# Find the minimum n that achieves target power
min_n_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- sample_sizes[min_n_idx]

# Verify power at this sample size and the preceding one
power_at_min_n <- calc_power(min_n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)
power_at_prev_n <- calc_power(min_n - 1, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)

cat("=== Sample Size Search ===\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Minimum n per group (integer):", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 6), "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev_n, 6), "\n\n")

# Display detailed results around the minimum
cat("=== Detailed Results Around Minimum n ===\n")
for (i in (min_n - 3):(min_n + 3)) {
  if (i > 0) {
    pw <- calc_power(i, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)
    meets <- ifelse(pw >= target_power, "✓", "✗")
    cat(sprintf("n = %3d: power = %.6f %s\n", i, pw, meets))
  }
}

cat("\n=== Final Answer ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group: ", min_n, "\n")
cat("Total participants (both groups): ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- list(
  sample_size = min_n,
  achieved_power = round(power_at_min_n, 6),
  power_at_preceding = round(power_at_prev_n, 6),
  effective_SD_participant_mean = round(effective_SD, 6),
  total_participants = 2 * min_n
)

cat("\nResults summary:\n")
print(results_json)

ICC <- 0.4
k <- 4  # observations per participant

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.9

# ===== CHECK 1: Effective variance of participant mean =====
# Under random intercept model with exchangeable correlation:
# Var(Yij) = σ² (marginal variance)
# Cov(Yij, Yij') = σ² * ICC for j ≠ j' (within same i)
# 
# The average of k observations: Ȳi = (1/k) * Σ_j Yij
# Var(Ȳi) = (1/k²) * Var(Σ_j Yij)
#         = (1/k²) * [k*σ² + k(k-1)*σ²*ICC]
#         = (1/k²) * σ² * [k + k(k-1)*ICC]
#         = (σ²/k) * [1 + (k-1)*ICC]

effective_var_formula1 <- (marginal_SD^2 / k) * (1 + (k - 1) * ICC)
effective_SD_formula1 <- sqrt(effective_var_formula1)

cat("=== CHECK 1: Effective SD of Participant Mean ===\n")
cat("Marginal SD (σ):", marginal_SD, "\n")
cat("ICC:", ICC, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Formula: Var(Ȳ) = (σ²/k) × [1 + (k-1)×ICC]\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ) =", marginal_SD^2, "/", k, "×", 
    paste0("[1 + ", k-1, "×", ICC, "]"), "\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ) =", marginal_SD^2/k, "×", 1 + (k-1)*ICC, "\n")
cat("Var(Ȳ) =", effective_var_formula1, "\n")
cat("SD(Ȳ) = √", effective_var_formula1, "=", effective_SD_formula1, "\n\n")

# ===== CHECK 2: Verify power formula using non-central t-test =====
# For two groups with equal n per group, analyzing participant averages:
# H0: μ1 = μ2
# HA: μ1 - μ2 = Δ (mean_diff)
#
# Test statistic: t = (Ȳ1 - Ȳ2) / SE(difference)
# SE(difference) = SD_pooled × √(2/n)
# Both groups have same effective SD, so SD_pooled = effective_SD
#
# Under HA:
# t ~ t(df = 2n-2) with non-centrality parameter λ = Δ / SE(difference)
# λ = mean_diff / (effective_SD × √(2/n))
#   = mean_diff × √(n/2) / effective_SD

calc_power_check <- function(n, delta, sigma, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  SE_diff <- sigma * sqrt(2 / n)
  lambda <- delta / SE_diff
  
  # Two-tailed power: P(T > t_crit | HA) + P(T < -t_crit | HA)
  power_upper <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  power_lower <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  power <- power_upper + power_lower
  
  return(list(
    df = df,
    t_crit = t_crit,
    SE_diff = SE_diff,
    lambda = lambda,
    power = power
  ))
}

# Two-group sample size calculation for repeated measures (participant averages)
# Analyzing participant means with pooled t-test

# Study parameters
marginal_SD <- 1          # Marginal SD of the outcome
ICC <- 0.4               # Intraclass correlation
k <- 4                   # Observations per participant
mean_diff <- 0.45        # Constant group mean difference
alpha <- 0.05            # Significance level
target_power <- 0.90     # Target power
allocation_ratio <- 1    # Equal allocation (1:1)

# Step 1: Calculate effective SD of participant averages
# When averaging k observations with ICC structure:
# Var(participant_mean) = (marginal_SD)^2 / k * [1 + (k-1)*ICC]

effective_var <- (marginal_SD^2 / k) * (1 + (k - 1) * ICC)
effective_SD <- sqrt(effective_var)

cat("=== Effective SD of Participant Averages ===\n")
cat("Marginal SD:", marginal_SD, "\n")
cat("ICC:", ICC, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Effective variance of participant mean:", effective_var, "\n")
cat("Effective SD of participant mean:", effective_SD, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Set up power calculation
# For a two-sample t-test comparing participant means:
# Under H0: μ1 = μ2
# Under HA: μ1 - μ2 = mean_diff
# 
# With equal allocation (n per group), the pooled SD is effective_SD
# The test statistic is t = (mean1 - mean2) / (SD_pooled * sqrt(2/n))
# where SD_pooled ≈ effective_SD (both groups have same marginal structure)
#
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = mean_diff / (effective_SD * sqrt(2/n))
# df = 2*n - 2

# Function to calculate power given n per group
calc_power <- function(n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  # Standard error of difference: SE = effective_SD * sqrt(2/n)
  SE_diff <- effective_SD * sqrt(2 / n)
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- mean_diff / SE_diff
  # Critical value (two-sided)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  # Power: P(|T| > t_crit | H_A)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Step 3: Find minimum n that achieves target power
# Search over a reasonable range
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) calc_power(n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha))

# Find the minimum n that achieves target power
min_n_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- sample_sizes[min_n_idx]

# Verify power at this sample size and the preceding one
power_at_min_n <- calc_power(min_n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)
power_at_prev_n <- calc_power(min_n - 1, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)

cat("=== Sample Size Search ===\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Minimum n per group (integer):", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 6), "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev_n, 6), "\n\n")

# Display detailed results around the minimum
cat("=== Detailed Results Around Minimum n ===\n")
for (i in (min_n - 3):(min_n + 3)) {
  if (i > 0) {
    pw <- calc_power(i, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)
    meets <- ifelse(pw >= target_power, "✓", "✗")
    cat(sprintf("n = %3d: power = %.6f %s\n", i, pw, meets))
  }
}

cat("\n=== Final Answer ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group: ", min_n, "\n")
cat("Total participants (both groups): ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- list(
  sample_size = min_n,
  achieved_power = round(power_at_min_n, 6),
  power_at_preceding = round(power_at_prev_n, 6),
  effective_SD_participant_mean = round(effective_SD, 6),
  total_participants = 2 * min_n
)

cat("\nResults summary:\n")
print(results_json)

# Two-group sample size calculation for repeated measures (participant averages)
# Analyzing participant means with pooled t-test

# Study parameters

ICC <- 0.4               # Intraclass correlation
k <- 4                   # Observations per participant
mean_diff <- 0.45        # Constant group mean difference
alpha <- 0.05            # Significance level
target_power <- 0.90     # Target power
allocation_ratio <- 1    # Equal allocation (1:1)

# Step 1: Calculate effective SD of participant averages
# When averaging k observations with ICC structure:
# Var(participant_mean) = (marginal_SD)^2 / k * [1 + (k-1)*ICC]

effective_var <- (marginal_SD^2 / k) * (1 + (k - 1) * ICC)
effective_SD <- sqrt(effective_var)

cat("=== Effective SD of Participant Averages ===\n")
cat("Marginal SD:", marginal_SD, "\n")
cat("ICC:", ICC, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Effective variance of participant mean:", effective_var, "\n")
cat("Effective SD of participant mean:", effective_SD, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Set up power calculation
# For a two-sample t-test comparing participant means:
# Under H0: μ1 = μ2
# Under HA: μ1 - μ2 = mean_diff
# 
# With equal allocation (n per group), the pooled SD is effective_SD
# The test statistic is t = (mean1 - mean2) / (SD_pooled * sqrt(2/n))
# where SD_pooled ≈ effective_SD (both groups have same marginal structure)
#
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = mean_diff / (effective_SD * sqrt(2/n))
# df = 2*n - 2

# Function to calculate power given n per group
calc_power <- function(n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  # Standard error of difference: SE = effective_SD * sqrt(2/n)
  SE_diff <- effective_SD * sqrt(2 / n)
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- mean_diff / SE_diff
  # Critical value (two-sided)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  # Power: P(|T| > t_crit | H_A)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Step 3: Find minimum n that achieves target power
# Search over a reasonable range
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) calc_power(n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha))

# Find the minimum n that achieves target power
min_n_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- sample_sizes[min_n_idx]

# Verify power at this sample size and the preceding one
power_at_min_n <- calc_power(min_n, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)
power_at_prev_n <- calc_power(min_n - 1, mean_diff, effective_SD, alpha)
